config.title: Event Handling

intro.title: Event Handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive counter application that responds to user clicks. You will learn how to handle events in React, such as button clicks, to update the state of your application. The core concepts covered include using event handlers like onClick, managing state with the useState hook, and updating the UI based on user interactions. By the end, you will understand how to make your React components dynamic and responsive to user input.
intro.usecase: Event handling is fundamental to every interactive React application you'll build. When users click buttons in e-commerce checkouts, type in search bars, or toggle settings in dashboards, event handlers respond to those actions. Developers implement onClick handlers for navigation menus, onSubmit for contact forms, and onChange for real-time filters in data tables. Mastering event handling allows you to create responsive interfaces that feel immediate and intuitive to users.

objectives: Implement event handlers in functional components using inline functions
Bind event handlers to JSX elements for user interactions like clicks and input changes
Construct controlled form inputs by updating state in response to events
Manipulate the DOM conditionally by integrating event-driven state changes
Configure event handlers to pass arguments without immediate invocation
Apply event object properties to access user input or element data
Initialize and update component state based on sequential user-triggered events

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns a JSX div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div element.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'App' and returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'App' and it returns a div element.

steps.title: Initialize state for a counter
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, declare a state variable named 'count' and initialize it to 0 using the useState hook.
steps.hint: Use array destructuring to get the state variable and setter function from useState(0).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: declaring a state variable
const [score, setScore] = useState(100);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a state variable 'count' initialized to 0, ready to be used in event handling.
successCriteria: The component contains a state declaration: const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0 and naming the variable 'count'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state declaration is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState(0) and destructure it as [count, setCount].

steps.title: Define an increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleIncrement that increases the count state by 1 using the setter function.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with count + 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function handleIncrement is defined that will update the count state when called.
successCriteria: The handleIncrement function is defined and uses setCount to increment count by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it uses setCount to increase count by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is not defined correctly. It should be named handleIncrement and update the count state.

steps.title: Add a heading to display the count
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an h1 element that displays the current count value.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to embed the count state variable inside the h1 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a heading that displays the current count value, which will update when state changes.
successCriteria: An h1 element is added inside the return statement that displays the count value using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an h1 element, but make sure it displays the count value using curly braces like {count}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element is missing or doesn't display the count value correctly. Check that you're using JSX curly braces to embed the state variable.

steps.title: Add a decrement button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Decrement' and wire its onClick event to call the handleDecrement function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the increment button. Use onClick={handleDecrement} to connect the event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A second button labeled 'Decrement' appears next to the increment button. When clicked, it decreases the count by 1.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Decrement' is added and its onClick prop is set to handleDecrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Decrement' and the onClick handler is properly set to handleDecrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a <button> with onClick={handleDecrement} and the text 'Decrement'.

steps.title: Define a reset handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named handleReset that sets the count state back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with 0 as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReset function is defined that will reset the counter to 0 when called.
successCriteria: The handleReset function is defined and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named handleReset and calls setCount(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleReset function isn't defined correctly. It should call setCount(0) to reset the count.

steps.title: Add a reset button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Reset' and wire its onClick event to the handleReset function you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Place the button after the decrement button in the JSX. Use the onClick prop and pass handleReset as the handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleReset}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A third button labeled 'Reset' appears in the UI. Clicking it resets the count to 0.
successCriteria: The JSX includes a <button> element with the text 'Reset' and an onClick prop set to handleReset.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might be missing the correct text or onClick handler. Make sure it says 'Reset' and uses onClick={handleReset}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset button is not correctly implemented. Check that you've added a <button> element with the text 'Reset' and onClick={handleReset}.
